summary: Victor A. van Bijlert worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earning his PhD from Leiden University (1975–1987). He held posts at NIAS, IIM Calcutta, Leiden University, and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam until 2021.

Historian Victor B. Lieberman studied at Yale (BA 1963–1967) and SOAS (PhD 1970–1976). Beginning in 1984, he served as Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History and Professor of Asian and Comparative History at the University of Michigan.

Tibetologist Victor Chan was a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He became Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia around 2002 and founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education in 2005.
Philosopher Victor Cousin studied at Lycée Charlemagne and the Pensionnat normal (around 1810–1812). He held a post at the University of Paris from around 1815 to 1851.

Victor Forte, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, received his PhD from Temple University in 2004. As attested in 2007, he served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor Goloubew studied at Saint Petersburg University and Heidelberg University (PhD 1901–1904). Working in archaeology and Indology, he held posts at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1920–1943).

Scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics Victor H. Mair studied at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD 1973–1976 under Patrick Hanan and James Robert Hightower). He taught at Harvard before joining the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Historian and linguist Victor Hehn studied at the University of Tartu (around 1830–1834). He held posts at the University of Tartu from around 1841 to 1851 and at the National Library of Russia from 1855 to 1873.

Linguist and Indologist Victor Henry studied at Strasbourg, Burgundy, and Paris under Abel Bergaigne. He held appointments at Lille, Douai, and the University of Paris, becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar at the Sorbonne in 1894.

Victor Herbert Jackson worked in archaeology and Indology. Joining the Indian Education Service in 1900, he taught at Presidency University (~1900–1907) and served as Principal of Patna College (~1907–1927).

Linguist Victor Michels studied in Berlin, Heidelberg, and Leipzig (PhD 1886–1889) under Paul Deussen, Hermann Osthoff, Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and Ernst Windisch. He served at the University of Göttingen and became Professor of German Philology at Jena in 1895.

Victor Turner studied at University College London and the University of Manchester (PhD ~1950–1955). Specializing in religious studies and anthropology, he held appointments at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.

Victoria Vertogradova, an Indologist and linguist, studied under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. Attested in 2026, she holds the post of chief research fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia studied at St. Xavier's College and Cambridge (PhD ~1963–1968). A scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, she held posts at Sydney, Hong Kong, SPA Delhi, the Smithsonian Institution, and Columbia University.

Indologist and linguist Vidya Niwas Mishra studied at Allahabad under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya, Gorakhpur, and under Paul Thieme. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Hindi Vidyapeeth, and was Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Vijay Singh, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned a Doctor of Philosophy from Panjab University (1998–2002). He was appointed Professor and Chairperson at Panjab University in 1994.
Vijaya Indra Suri was an active scholar in Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijaya Dharma Suri, as attested in 1933. He also founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Vijayalakshmi Mani works in the fields of Indology and archaeology. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Viktor Iosifovich Balin, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1946 to 1951. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University beginning in 1952.
